newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Stg/mark easily holds above three marks in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark easily holds above three marks in Asia.

text.p: Sterling was holding at levels comfortably above three marks in quiet Asian trading on Monday after its surge above the three mark barrier in European trade on Friday, dealers said.
At 0400 GMT it was quoted in Asia at 3.0045/55 compared with late London quotes of around 2.9975 marks. Earlier on Monday it hit a high of 3.0090, before drifting back.
On Friday, sterling hit a peak of 3.0010 marks in London, its strongest level against the German unit in over 6-1/2 years.

Sterling has been bolstered by rising interest rates, a strong economy and its safe haven status amid turmoil generated by approaching European Economic and Monetary Union, set for launch in January, 1999.
Base U.K. lending rates were nudged up for the third month running last week to 6.75 percent and analysts say there are more interest rate rises in the pipeline.
However, Germany has an economy that is stuttering at best and a much lower interest rate regime, which makes its currency unattractive to foreign exchange market traders.
Three month sterling deposits are around seven percent while the same rate for the German mark is about 3-1/16 percent.
"Three marks was always the target for sterling and it's made it," said the head of trading at a European bank in Singapore.
"I'm not a natural sterling bull at the moment, but I'd hate to be fighting the market on this one," he added.
The sterling trader at another European bank in Singapore said his philosophy would remain the same for the pound as when it was approaching three marks.
"It worked all the way up from 2.50 marks or so. You just buy on the dips and take profit when it gets ahead of itself," he said.
Trading in Asia was not especially active on Monday morning, he said.
"There's still a lingering feeling that the Old Lady (the Bank of England) won't exactly be happy to see sterling above three marks -- it's a pretty crucial psychological level," he said.
"Certainly there's been no sign of any intervention, but it's definitely a background factor since the market out here is so thin," he added.
The head of trading said he expected to see sterling/mark head to around 3.0500/0600 in the near future -- assuming no central bank intervention.
